web/composer/guided/chat_solver.py:R2:_a: `_admit_deferred_intent_repair_thread` is the ADR-032 parse boundary for raw LiteLLM response objects (Tier-3: provider-returned, shape-unguaranteed). Its `message` and `tool_call` arguments are pydantic models whose tool-call fields live in `extra="allow"` storage and resolve dynamically, so a nominal `isinstance` against an owned class is impossible and a bare attribute read would raise `AttributeError` out of the guided chat loop on any provider whose payload omits the field. ADR-032's prescribed form for exactly this case is sentinel `getattr` + value assertion + construction of an owned type, which is what this function does: every extracted value is checked with `type(x) is not str` (or an explicit sentinel/None comparison) and the function returns `None` — never a fabricated default — when any check fails, after which the owned frozen carriers `_DeferredIntentRepairThread` / `_RepairThreadToolCall` / `_RepairThreadToolFunction` are the only shapes replay touches. The default is the module-private sentinel `_MISSING_REPAIR_THREAD_FIELD = object()`, which is not a value any provider payload can produce, so absence stays distinguishable from a legitimately-`None` field. What it protects: `_deferred_intent_repair_thread` re-materialises the assistant turn and MUST answer every tool-call id (the OpenAI/LiteLLM protocol 400s on an unanswered id); admitting a partially readable provider turn would emit a malformed repair thread instead of falling back to the caller's retention path via `raise retain_failures[0][1]`. This site reads `message.content`. The value is asserted on the next line — it must be the sentinel-free `None` or an exact `str` (`assistant_content is not None and type(assistant_content) is not str` returns `None`) — before it is carried as `_DeferredIntentRepairThread.assistant_content` and re-emitted as the assistant turn's `content`. A missing `content` attribute and a legitimate `content=None` are different facts here, and only the sentinel keeps them apart: `None` is admitted, absence is refused.

web/composer/guided/chat_solver.py:R6:ma: This handler is the accumulator-append validator shape, not a swallow. R6 fires because `_handler_is_silent` treats only `raise`, a non-default `return`, and a non-default `yield` as explicit outcomes, and this handler instead appends `(retain_call, exc)` to the local `retain_failures` accumulator and falls off the end. The caught exception is narrow and typed (`DeferredIntentActionShapeError`, raised by `_parse_deferred_intent_tool_arguments` at the Tier-3 boundary that decodes untrusted `retain_deferred_intent` tool-call JSON), and it is consumed, never lost: the `if retain_failures:` block immediately below is the control. It either re-raises the first captured exception verbatim — `raise retain_failures[0][1]`, taken when `deferred_repair_used` is already set, when the attempt budget is exhausted, or when `_admit_deferred_intent_repair_thread` returns `None` because the provider turn cannot be faithfully re-materialised — or it threads every captured exception back to the model as value-free shape rejections via `_deferred_intent_repair_thread(admitted_repair, errors=tuple(exc for _, exc in retain_failures))` and records `ComposerLLMCallStatus.MALFORMED_RESPONSE` with `error_class = type(retain_failures[0][1]).__name__` on the audited call. Collecting per-call failures before deciding is load-bearing: the loop must attempt EVERY retain call so the repair thread can answer every tool-call id, and re-raising inside the handler would abandon the already-parsed sibling actions and skip the bounded self-repair the composer relies on. This is the Step 1 (resolve_source) copy. Its `if retain_failures:` block additionally passes `admitted_repair = None` when `is_withheld_retained_group` holds — a form-directed revision in which the provider replayed a withheld `resolve_source` call — which forces the `raise retain_failures[0][1]` arm, so the withheld mutation is never parsed or applied.
